design.rule.accentHues.why: when there are more than a few accent colours, none of them is an accent
design.rule.animatedLayout.why: Every frame recomputes the position of the neighbours — the animation stutters and everything around it jumps.
design.rule.animationFast.message: the motion lasts {ms} ms, below the {min} ms threshold
design.rule.animationFast.why: the eye registers that something happened but not what — it reads as a glitch rather than a transition
design.rule.animationSlow.message: the animation runs {ms} ms, the limit is {limit} ms
design.rule.animationSlow.why: past the limit motion stops reading as a response and starts reading as a wait
design.rule.autocomplete.message: a field for a value the browser knows, with no autocomplete (expected «{token}»)
design.rule.autocomplete.why: an address and a phone number have been typed a hundred times already; refusing autofill means typing them again, with a typo
design.rule.borderInvisible.message: the border almost merges with the background (contrast {ratio})
design.rule.borderInvisible.why: the border is declared, takes up layout space, and does not do its only job — separating
design.rule.brokenImage.why: An empty frame or a broken-image icon stands where the picture should be — the page looks broken.
design.rule.canonicalMissing.why: The same page at several addresses competes with itself.
design.rule.canonicalRelative.why: A relative canonical resolves differently on each host, so the copies point at each other instead of at one address.
design.rule.charset.message: the page charset is {charset} rather than UTF-8
design.rule.charset.why: Anything but UTF-8 will one day meet a character it lacks and show garbage instead.
design.rule.clipped.message: Content is {overflow}px wider than its container and is clipped
design.rule.clipped.why: Part of the text or the controls cannot be seen or reached by scrolling.
design.rule.clones.why: Clone cards of the same size and structure are filler, not content.
design.rule.contrast.why: Text at this contrast is unreadable in bright light and for people with low vision.
design.rule.contrastState.why: At rest the element reads, under the cursor or in focus it does not: the text is lost exactly where the person is looking.
design.rule.copySlop.why: Tells of machine writing in the page copy say nothing about the product and read as filler. The catalogue is the one the text check uses; project rules live in .vibe/slop.json.
design.rule.deadStateContract.evidence: {contract} on “{name}”: after the click neither the attribute, the look nor the content changed
design.rule.deadStateContract.message: The control declares {contract}, but a click changes nothing
design.rule.deadStateContract.why: A declared state is a promise: a screen reader says «sorted ascending» while nothing is sorted.
design.rule.descriptionLong.message: the description is longer than {max}: {length} characters
design.rule.descriptionLong.why: The tail gets cut with an ellipsis, and the sentence breaks mid-thought.
design.rule.descriptionMissing.why: The description is the second line in search results; without it a random fragment of the page goes there.
design.rule.descriptionShort.message: the description is shorter than {min}: {length} characters
design.rule.descriptionShort.why: Too short a description does not explain why one should come in.
design.rule.disabledLook.why: A person clicks, nothing happens, and they conclude the interface is broken.
design.rule.errorLink.evidence: aria-invalid=true, aria-describedby is empty or points nowhere
design.rule.errorLink.message: The field is marked invalid but no explanation is linked to it
design.rule.errorLink.why: A screen reader says “invalid value” and stops: what exactly is wrong is never spoken.
design.rule.errorText.message: the field is marked invalid, but there is no error text
design.rule.errorText.why: a red border says «wrong» and never says «what exactly» — the person starts guessing
design.rule.extremeRadius.why: A radius this large stops being a rounding and becomes a shape — usually by accident.
design.rule.eyebrow.message: An eyebrow chip above the headline
design.rule.eyebrow.why: All-caps in a pill before a headline is a template-landing cliché that carries no meaning.
design.rule.favicon.why: People find a tab by its icon; without one it is a nameless rectangle among twenty identical ones.
design.rule.fieldLabel.message: a field with no label — what goes in it is only implied by context
design.rule.fieldLabel.why: a label is the only thing that survives autofill, an error and a return to the form; a guess from nearby text survives nothing
design.rule.fieldName.message: the field has no name attribute
design.rule.fieldName.why: the browser has nothing to remember and nothing to fill in, and a plain form submit drops the value silently
design.rule.fieldNarrow.message: the field is {width}px wide, the minimum is {min}px
design.rule.fieldNarrow.why: in a narrow field the value scrolls out of sight while it is being typed and cannot be re-read before submitting
design.rule.focusContrast.message: the focus ring is at {ratio} contrast, at least {min} is needed
design.rule.focusContrast.why: to someone navigating by keyboard an invisible ring is the same as a removed one: nothing on the screen answers «where am I»
design.rule.focusRing.message: The focus ring is removed and nothing replaces it
design.rule.focusRing.why: From the keyboard there is no way to see where you are: the page becomes impassable without a mouse.
design.rule.fontScale.message: the page has {count} distinct font sizes, {max} being reasonable
design.rule.fontScale.why: A scale is a decision; a dozen sizes is what happens when every component picked its own.
design.rule.fonts.why: More than two families is a page assembled from two different designs.
design.rule.glass.why: Glass almost always lowers the contrast of text on the layer and is expensive while scrolling.
design.rule.glow.message: A glow instead of a shadow
design.rule.glow.why: A shadow with no offset means light from nowhere — the object stops resting on a surface.
design.rule.gradientText.message: The headline is filled with a gradient
design.rule.gradientText.why: Gradient text is the most recognisable tell of a generated page, and it reads worse too.
design.rule.h1Missing.why: The h1 answers «what is this about»; without it the page starts straight from the details.
design.rule.h1Multiple.why: Two main subjects are none: the reader cannot tell which one is theirs.
design.rule.hangingPreposition.message: Hanging preposition: {count} lines end with a short word
design.rule.hangingPreposition.why: A preposition torn from its word trips the reading — in Russian typesetting this is a rule, not taste.
design.rule.headingSkip.message: A heading level was skipped: h{from} → h{to}
design.rule.headingSkip.why: A screen reader builds an outline from headings — a gap breaks navigation of the page.
design.rule.hover.why: With a mouse the response confirms the control is alive; on touch there is none at all — hence a hint, not a defect.
design.rule.hoverSnap.message: hover changes the look abruptly — there is no transition
design.rule.hoverSnap.why: the jump is visible but its cause is not: without a transition the eye does not link the change to its own mouse movement
design.rule.iconButton.evidence: no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no text
design.rule.iconButton.message: An icon button with no accessible name
design.rule.iconButton.why: A screen reader will just say “button” — what it does cannot be learned.
design.rule.iconContrast.message: the icon is at {ratio} contrast, at least {min} is needed
design.rule.iconContrast.why: an unlabelled icon carries the meaning by itself; at decoration contrast that meaning cannot be read
design.rule.imageAlt.message: The image has no alt attribute
design.rule.imageAlt.why: A screen reader will read out the file name; an empty alt="" is a legitimate “decorative image”.
design.rule.infinite.message: an endless animation on something that is not a wait indicator
design.rule.infinite.why: endless motion is a claim on attention that never expires: the eye keeps going back to it whatever the page says
design.rule.inputType.message: the field is left as plain text, expected type «{type}»
design.rule.inputType.why: on a phone the type picks the keyboard: digits of a phone number on a text keyboard cost two taps each
design.rule.invisibleState.evidence: was {before}, became {after}, look and content unchanged
design.rule.invisibleState.message: The {contract} state changes while the screen stays the same
design.rule.invisibleState.why: A sighted person sees nothing: they pressed it and cannot tell whether it worked.
design.rule.langMissing.message: the <html> element has no lang attribute
design.rule.langMissing.why: Without a language a screen reader speaks the text with the wrong phonetics, and the browser offers to translate what needs no translation.
design.rule.lineHeight.loose: line height {ratio} — the paragraph falls apart into separate lines
design.rule.lineHeight.tight: line height {ratio} — the lines stick together
design.rule.lineHeight.why: Line height is what keeps a paragraph a paragraph: too tight makes it a wall, too loose makes it a list.
design.rule.lineLong.message: a line of about {chars} characters, past the {max} limit
design.rule.lineLong.why: On a long line the eye loses where to return at the end: reading becomes physically harder.
design.rule.linearEasing.message: linear easing on a one-shot animation
design.rule.linearEasing.why: nothing in the physical world starts at full speed, so linear motion reads as mechanical
design.rule.linkColorOnly.message: a link inside text is told apart by colour alone
design.rule.linkColorOnly.why: to a colour-blind reader such a link is plain text — that is, the page has no links at all
design.rule.linkSameColor.message: the link is the same colour as the text around it
design.rule.linkSameColor.why: even a sighted reader cannot find it: there is no difference at all, only sweeping the cursor at random
design.rule.noindex.message: the page is closed from indexing (noindex)
design.rule.noindex.why: Almost always a leftover from a staging build: the page exists and cannot be found.
design.rule.occluded.message: The text is covered by an opaque layer “{selector}”
design.rule.occluded.why: The content is in the markup but invisible — the reader concludes it is gone.
design.rule.ogTitle.why: A link sent to a messenger unfurls as a URL instead of a name — and nobody clicks it.
design.rule.orphan.evidence: {total} lines, one word in the last
design.rule.orphan.message: A single word on the last line
design.rule.orphan.why: A word left hanging under a paragraph looks like a fragment — the reader looks for a continuation.
design.rule.outsideForm.message: the field is not inside a form
design.rule.outsideForm.why: Enter submits nothing and the browser does not offer to save what was entered — the familiar gestures stop working
design.rule.overshoot.why: A bounce belongs in a game and hinders a tool: it delays the very thing that was clicked for.
design.rule.pageOverflow.message: The page is {overflow}px wider than the window — horizontal scrolling appeared
design.rule.pageOverflow.why: Horizontal scrolling on a phone breaks reading: lines run off the edge.
design.rule.placeholderDuplicate.message: the placeholder repeats the label word for word
design.rule.placeholderDuplicate.why: the hint slot is taken by what is already written next to it — an example of the format will not fit there any more
design.rule.placeholderLabel.message: The field has only a placeholder instead of a label
design.rule.placeholderLabel.why: The placeholder disappears on input: a filled form becomes a row of nameless rectangles.
design.rule.pressFeedback.message: the control gives nothing back while pressed (no :active rule)
design.rule.pressFeedback.why: on a phone there is no hover at all — the press is the only feedback between the tap and the result
design.rule.pureBlack.why: maximum contrast is not maximum readability: on a bright screen such text halates and tires the eye
design.rule.purple.message: The palette rests on purple ({purple} of {colored} coloured surfaces)
design.rule.purple.why: The purple-blue gradient is the default palette of generators; a product wearing it is indistinguishable from the next one.
design.rule.radiusDrift.message: Radius drift: {count} different radii on the page
design.rule.radiusDrift.why: The radius scale is part of the system; five near-identical values read as an accident, not a decision.
design.rule.readOnlyLook.message: the field is read-only, but the cursor over it is a text caret
design.rule.readOnlyLook.why: the caret is a promise that says «type here»; typing changes nothing, and the person looks for their own mistake
design.rule.reducedMotion.message: the page is animated ({count} elements), but no stylesheet answers prefers-reduced-motion
design.rule.reducedMotion.why: for a person with a vestibular disorder full-screen motion is nausea, and the system setting means they have already asked
design.rule.reducedMotionHides.evidence: opacity {opacity} with the animation silenced by the reduce block
design.rule.reducedMotionHides.message: The content is invisible before its animation, and reduced motion turns that animation off
design.rule.reducedMotionHides.why: Someone who asked for less motion gets not a calmer page but an empty one: the element stays transparent.
design.rule.requiredDisabled.message: the field is required and disabled at the same time
design.rule.requiredDisabled.why: the form can never be submitted, and nothing on the page explains why
design.rule.requiredVisual.message: The field's requiredness is declared only by an asterisk in the label
design.rule.requiredVisual.why: The asterisk is read out as a character mid-sentence — requiredness is not conveyed by ear.
design.rule.saturatedArea.message: a saturated fill over {share}% of the screen (saturation {saturation}%)
design.rule.saturatedArea.why: over a large area a saturated colour vibrates, and everything on top of it loses legibility
design.rule.shouting.message: a {length}-character phrase is set in capitals
design.rule.shouting.why: All caps reads slower, letter by letter, and sounds like shouting even where nobody meant to shout.
design.rule.spacing.why: Values off the step are the ones typed by hand while everything else came from tokens; the eye reads it as unevenness.
design.rule.tapTarget.why: A finger cannot hit a target this small: a miss reads as “the interface is broken”.
design.rule.textColors.message: text colours on the page: {count}, the sensible limit is {limit}
design.rule.textColors.why: a palette drifts one hex at a time and every step looks fine — only counting shows it
design.rule.textOnImage.message: the text lies straight on a photograph, with no scrim and no shadow
design.rule.textOnImage.why: the contrast here cannot be computed at all: it depends on the pixel under each letter, and tomorrow the photograph will be replaced by a lighter one
design.rule.tinyText.message: Font size {size}px — below the minimum of {min}px
design.rule.tinyText.why: Such text cannot be read on a phone without zooming.
design.rule.titleLong.message: the title is longer than {max}: {length} characters
design.rule.titleLong.why: The tail gets cut, and it gets cut exactly where the important part usually sits.
design.rule.titleMissing.why: The title is what shows in the tab, in bookmarks and in search results; without it the page is named by its URL.
design.rule.titleShort.message: the title is too short: {length} characters
design.rule.titleShort.why: A short title does not tell the page from its neighbours — neither in search results nor among twenty open tabs.
design.rule.transitionAll.why: the list picks up properties nobody chose, including the ones that relayout the page every frame
design.rule.transitionSlow.message: the transition runs {ms} ms, the limit is {limit} ms
design.rule.transitionSlow.why: an interface that trails the cursor by half a second feels slow no matter how fast the code is
design.rule.viewportMissing.why: A phone renders the page as a desktop one and scales it down to unreadable.
design.rule.viewportZoom.why: Blocking zoom takes away the only way to read small text from the person for whom it is small.

settings.agent.hint.audit: A log of the agent's actions in .vibe/audit.jsonl (prompts, replies, tool calls, gates). Arguments, command bodies and file contents are never written — only the tool name and the outcome.
settings.agent.hint.checksLimitsHint: Files beyond the count or size limit are not scanned; the skip is reported in the chat feed.
settings.agent.hint.checksModes: Deterministic checks of the files a turn changed: a leaked secret and a write to a protected path. off / notify / enforce (send the agent back). No LLM judge is involved.
settings.agent.hint.compaction: <html>Old tool results are dropped first — the model's answers stay. Only if that is not enough are the earliest messages folded into a summary. Tool schemas count too: they travel in every request.</html>
settings.agent.hint.contextFilter: auto — collapse repeats and drop noise (progress bars, separators); raw — leave it alone; aggregate — keep only the shape (which line occurred how many times); off — same as raw. Noise is not merely large: it teaches the model that repetition is the point of the output, and it pushes the real error out of the window.
settings.agent.hint.contextHint: Invisible characters (including Unicode tags, which render as nothing at all) and bidi overrides are ALWAYS stripped from the context — they do not occur in honest code, and a person approving a change cannot see an instruction hidden in them. Text that looks like an address to the agent, and secrets, are marked with a “🛡 контекст” line in the feed. This switch additionally replaces the secret value itself with a marker in what is sent to the model; the file on disk is never changed. Off by default: an agent often needs to work with a config that legitimately contains a token.
settings.agent.hint.council: Format: provider/model separated by commas, e.g. zai/glm-4.6, minimax/abab6. DIFFERENT models are required: the same one asked twice agrees with itself, and the second answer looks like confirmation without being one. Invoked with /council <question>: advisers answer in parallel, blind to each other, and a turn then reconciles them. Empty turns the council off.
settings.agent.hint.designHint: After a turn that changed interface files (.tsx, .css, .svg… — tests do not count) the page is measured in the “Design” tool window. notify — a summary in the feed, the turn ends either way. enforceFloor — the agent keeps working while quality-floor findings remain (contrast, tap targets, clipping): taste findings never block, otherwise an opinion would become a blocker and produce loops about style. If the “Design” panel is closed, the gate says so instead of staying silent.
settings.agent.hint.digest: Empty means off. At the set time the IDE sends a short digest: how many runs, what failed, how much was spent and which role spent most. It answers three questions and no more: a digest that tries to tell everything becomes a report, and a report is not read either. If the IDE was closed, the digest arrives when it opens — but only within two hours of the scheduled time: yesterday’s digest at noon is noise.
settings.agent.hint.directTools: <html>The model searches the project and reads the shared memory by itself; recording a decision or changing the memory needs your consent. The memory needs VibeMemory installed.</html>
settings.agent.hint.embedding: Format provider/model, e.g. openai/text-embedding-3-small or a local Ollama model. Empty turns semantic search off. The index is built with /index and stored in the IDE system path rather than the repository: vectors are regenerable, large and personal to whoever paid for them. Rebuilds are incremental — by file size and modification time — because re-embedding a repository for every question costs real money.
settings.agent.hint.failover: `provider/model` separated by commas. Used only when waiting has already failed: the IDE first waits out the provider’s limit and moves on only after the retries are exhausted. A bad key never fails over — the key is wrong at the next provider too, and switching would hide the real message behind an unrelated failure. No target is tried twice in one turn.
settings.agent.hint.fimHint: Works with models marked fim: true in the provider catalogue (openai protocol). Context is 25 lines around the caret, 12 for a local model: there every token costs time. In some places no request is sent at all (the caret at the start of a line with someone else's code to the right) — such a suggestion would be noise anyway. The answer is cleaned of explanations and comments in another language; counters and p50/p95 latency are in the “VibeIDEA: autocomplete metrics” action.
settings.agent.hint.foreignHint: One line the first time a project is opened: the contents of someone else's repository are data, not commands. Nothing is blocked and it does not repeat.
settings.agent.hint.handshakeHint: How long to wait for the agent to answer initialize/session/new. A cold start through npx can be slow.
settings.agent.hint.hooks: Commands from .vibe/hooks.json around the agent's tool calls. They run only in a trusted project and only while this switch is on.
settings.agent.hint.httpApiHint: Lets you start the agent from CI, a bot or a cron job: POST /run with a task, GET /health for a liveness check. ONLY the loopback address is listened on — there is no “listen externally” setting and there will not be. Every request needs a token (Authorization: Bearer …); the token lives in the OS keychain and is shown by the “VibeIDEA: show HTTP API token” action. The task is performed by the agent in an open window; changes apply immediately, without restarting the IDE. Spec: docs/vibe/manuals/httpApiSpec.md.
settings.agent.hint.mcpClasses: Reading MCP tools (import graph, corpus search, symbol usages) are always available. Writing and starting work are separate switches, off by default: turning on the HTTP API for the import graph should not hand out agent runs as well. In a project not marked as trusted, writing and starting work stay closed whatever the switches say.
settings.agent.hint.metricPattern: A regular expression with one group, e.g. «Total time: ([0-9.]+)». Empty means any number. The LAST match wins: a build prints numbers along the way and the summary people read comes at the end. The direction (lower or higher is better) is set separately and decided BEFORE the work: deciding afterwards is how a regression becomes a success.
settings.agent.hint.minimalism: off — do not interfere; light — «reuse what exists first»; full — plus no abstraction for a single case, no wrapper around a single call, no comment restating code; ultra — plus every line must be necessary. A ladder rather than a switch: a prototype and a payment path want different discipline. What has accumulated can be reviewed with /simplify, which reads the current diff as a delete list.
settings.agent.hint.offline: Nothing leaves the machine: no cloud model requests, no embeddings. Local providers (localhost) keep working. This is not about traffic but about a promise: some projects cannot let file contents leave the machine, and such a promise must be kept by a mechanism rather than by memory — so the check sits at the single door out, not in the interface.
settings.agent.hint.proxy: For example http://proxy.local:3128 or socks5://127.0.0.1:9050; the port may be omitted. This is a SEPARATE proxy from the system one and the IDE one: reaching the plugin repository and reaching a model provider are different questions, and people routinely need one without the other. Empty means model requests take the same route as the whole IDE (Settings → HTTP Proxy: the IDE proxy, the system one or a direct connection); a typo is logged rather than silently ignored.
settings.agent.hint.proxyDirect: The ticked providers and external agents reach their servers directly: past the model proxy and past the IDE proxy. The rest go through the model proxy, or the IDE route when it is empty. An external agent gets its route as HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY and NO_PROXY at start; a variable in the agent entry's env wins. An automatic IDE proxy (PAC, autodetection) cannot be handed to an agent — set the model proxy explicitly.
settings.agent.hint.reasoning: off / low / medium / high. Every vendor named this differently: Anthropic takes a token budget on older models and an effort level on newer ones, OpenAI a word, Gemini its own budget. One slider is honest only if translated into each dialect: reasoning_effort sent to Anthropic does nothing, silently, and the user concludes the setting is decorative. The budget always leaves room for the answer — a budget equal to max_tokens is rejected by the API, and that looks like «the model says nothing». Some models DO NOT ALLOW turning reasoning off (Kimi K3, GLM-5.3, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable and Mythos 5, GPT-6 Astra): for them «off» takes the lowest level rather than switching off, and the reasoning is billed at the OUTPUT rate — $15 per million for K3 against $3 for input (platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing, checked 20.09.2026). For those models the slider saves nothing; choosing another model does. Models that reason by default (Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5, GPT-6 Sol and Luna, MiMo v2.6) get the vendor's explicit switch on «off» — without it they would reason at their default. MiMo has no levels at all: low, medium and high are the same thing for it — reasoning on.
settings.agent.hint.roleBudget: 0 means no limit. Counted per role over a rolling day rather than per run: the ruinous case is not one expensive turn but a reviewer restarted forty times by a loop. Checked BEFORE the step; at 80% the chat warns, at 100% the step is skipped. The report is the «VibeIDEA: spend by role» command.
settings.agent.hint.runsHint: The “Dispatcher” panel shows runs nobody was watching: incoming HTTP API tasks and pipelines. Ordinary conversation is not recorded here — it has the chat history. Only metadata goes into the ledger: goal, status, steps, number of changed files, times; no prompts, no model replies, no tool arguments. An unfinished run is never removed by age or by the record cap — otherwise the trace of something that may still be running would disappear.
settings.agent.hint.silence: 0 turns it off. At this mark the chat says there is no sign of life; at twice it, the turn is ended as hung. A hung turn looks exactly like a thinking one: same spinner, same silence. The loop detector works separately and always: four identical calls in a row, or a repeating cycle (read A → edit B → read A…), stop the turn with a breaker — from the inside every step of a loop looks reasonable, and only someone counting from outside notices.
settings.agent.hint.slopHint: After a turn in which the agent wrote text for people (.md, .txt, .rst…), the detector reads those files. notify: a line in the feed when the text does not pass. enforce: the agent goes back to the text until it passes, but no more than the set number of times. Text that passes is silence. Project rules live in .vibe/slop.json.
settings.agent.hint.slopRuleBudgetHint: How long one rule of the detector may search a text. A pattern from .vibe/slop.json with nested repetition (((a+)+)+b) doubles its time with every character and would hang the IDE; a rule past the limit is dropped for the rest of the check and named in the result. The built-in catalogue checks a megabyte of text in under three seconds with all its rules.
settings.agent.hint.telegram: The project is where tasks from the bot chat go (empty means the first open window). The proxy is separate from the model proxy: Telegram and model APIs are blocked in different places by different people. The bot token is set with «VibeIDEA: Telegram bot token» and lives in the OS secure storage, not here.
settings.agent.hint.terminalHint: Claude's live command output is always shown. This switch lets THIRD-PARTY agents (Gemini CLI and others) execute commands through the standard ACP terminal/… methods — with a timeout clamp, output trimming and confirmation of destructive commands.
settings.agent.hint.verifyCommandHint: For example ./bazel.cmd test //… or npm run verify. Empty means the gate does nothing.
settings.agent.hint.verifyModes: A build/test check at the end of a turn that changed files. off — disabled; warn — reports; enforce — “not done until it is green”: the agent is sent back to work up to the attempt limit.
settings.agent.hint.watch: Subtitles are taken from the site by this comma-separated language list (e.g. ru,en). Frames are captured at scene changes rather than at equal intervals: they are the key moments, not an even sample, and more frames means a more expensive turn.

settings.agent.hint.terse: The model answers without filler: no pleasantries, hedging or narration of its own steps, while terms, code and error texts stay verbatim. Code, comments, commits and documents are written in normal language, warnings and confirmations of irreversible actions in full sentences. Lite drops only filler, full also uses short phrases, ultra is as short as possible. The instruction is based on the Caveman skill (MIT). The same choice is in the quick-settings button of the composer row.

settings.lsp.hint: The path to the SERVER'S OWN executable — not to node and not to php: whatever is written here becomes the whole start command. Empty means the usual resolution: your server from PATH, then the bundled one. Fill it in when the server lives outside PATH: vendor/bin, a shared container folder, a build from source. A .js script is started by the interpreter from the field above. A path that stopped working is named by the doctor.
settings.lsp.interpreterInField: ⚠ this names an interpreter {path}, not a server: the path becomes the whole start command, and the server would start as node --stdio, without the script itself. Clear the field — Node belongs in «Node interpreter» above.
settings.lsp.node.bad: The path you named cannot be run: {path} — no server will start until it is fixed or cleared
settings.lsp.node.hint: Empty means «find it yourself». The order: the project's .nvmrc → nvm → fnm → volta → asdf → your shell's PATH → Homebrew, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin (on Windows, Program Files and AppData\Roaming\npm). A path named here beats all of it. An application started from Finder does not inherit the shell's PATH, which is why a Node installed by a version manager could be invisible without this page. No need to set a per-project version here: an .nvmrc in the project root is read on its own.
settings.lsp.node.missing: No Node interpreter found — TypeScript, ESLint, CSS and the JavaScript debugger will not start. Install Node or name its path here.
settings.lsp.php.hint: The bundled Phpactor works on every system, Windows included: its phar demanded the posix extension, which no Windows build of PHP has, but the requirement turned out to be false — every posix call inside is guarded, and the IDE switches the check off itself. Intelephense is optional: it runs on Node and installs with npm install -g intelephense; its free tier covers completion, go to definition, find references, diagnostics and formatting.

settings.lsp.ts.hint: TypeScript 7 — the compiler rewritten in Go — speaks LSP itself (tsc --lsp --stdio) and loads a large project several times faster. Its native server ships in the project's own typescript package, so the IDE downloads and bundles nothing: a project on TypeScript 7 already has the server. “Automatic” takes the project's tsc when node_modules holds typescript 7 or newer, and the bundled vtsls otherwise — TypeScript 5 and 6 have no --lsp mode. A hand-picked tsc the project does not have falls back to vtsls, and the language servers doctor names the reason.

settings.root.html:
VibeIDEA settings
Providers — API keys and the status of their check.
Models — which models appear in the pickers.

Registry on disk: the .vibe/providers/*.jsonc folder (the active toggle) plus providers.json on top, at the global ~/.vibe and project levels; keys live only in the OS secure storage or in .vibe/.env.
settings.sound.hint: The built-in chime is synthesised on the spot: no assets, no dependencies, and it sounds the same on every platform. A custom file is validated by trying to open it rather than by its extension — what the JDK can play depends on the machine. By default the sound stays silent while the window is focused: it is meant for someone who looked away, and beeping at a person watching the screen ends with the sound being turned off for good. Events in a row (pipeline steps) are merged by a 1.5-second window.
